detail: FreeBMD, FreeCEN and FreeREG, read 18 October 2026 without an account. Findmypast had signed out in the browser and no password was entered. FreeBMD gave the marriage and the deaths; FreeCEN gave the 1851 census; FreeREG gave the baptisms and marriages at Weston, Hertfordshire.

FreeBMD, Hitchin, vol 6 p711, March quarter 1851 (over 99 per cent transcribed). A search of Hitchin for any Joseph Wallis, 1848 to 1853, returns this entry alone. Every surname on that page, read by a search on the volume and page: Bigg Charlotte, Dearman George, Field Sarah, Wallis Joseph. Two couples; Bigg and Dearman are one, and Field and Wallis are the other. THE SPOUSE IS INFERRED FROM THE PAGE, NOT NAMED BY THE INDEX.

HO 107 piece 1709, ED 10c, folio 190, page 30, schedule 117 (FreeCEN). JOSEPH WALLIS, head, married, 23, agricultural labourer, born Weston; SARAH, wife, 21, born Weston; JAMES FIELD, lodger, unmarried, 24, agricultural labourer, born Weston.

Same piece, ED 10c, folio 184, page 19, schedule 81. MARY WALLIS, head, widow, 42, 'pauper labourer's widow', born Wallington; EMMA 21, ANN 17, HESTHER 15, ELIZA 9, all straw plaiters; JEREMIAH 6, WILLIAM 3, ELIZA ANN 1 (granddaughter); ABLE WATSON, lodger. No Joseph; he had a house of his own.

FreeREG, Weston Holy Trinity (transcribed by a volunteer; the entry is line 491): Joseph, son of WILLIAM and MARY WALLIS, labourer, of Weston. The only Joseph Wallis baptised at Weston in a search of 1825 to 1833; one born in 1822 is the son of George and Betsey.

record: Marriage, William Wallis and Mary Foster, 10 February 1827
detail: FreeREG, Weston Holy Trinity: William Wallis, bachelor, of Weston, and Mary Foster, spinster, of Weston; witnesses James Watson and William Kent. Joseph's baptism follows by five months. Of four William Wallis marriages in Hertfordshire from 1815 to 1830 this is the only one at Weston.

record: Baptisms to William and Mary Wallis at Weston
detail: Eliza 6 Nov 1842; Jeremiah 5 Oct 1845; William 7 May 1848 (all FreeREG, father a labourer). The widow's household of 1851 holds an Eliza of 9, a Jeremiah of 6 and a William of 3: the names match and each census age is one year over the baptism. Emma, Ann and Hesther of that household were not found as baptisms in the same search.

FreeREG, Weston Holy Trinity: Sarah, daughter of WILLIAM and ELIZABETH FIELD, labourer. Brothers and sisters baptised to the same parents: Emma 23 May 1824, JAMES 25 Feb 1827, Charlotte 4 Nov 1832. Every Field baptism at Weston in the index for 1824 to 1833 was read, eight in all, and the other four belong to other couples.

record: Marriage, William Field and Elizabeth Phillips, 2 June 1823
detail: FreeREG, Weston Holy Trinity: William Field, bachelor, of Weston, and Elizabeth Phillips, spinster, of Weston; witnesses James Wallis and Mary Warren. Of seven William Field marriages in Hertfordshire from 1815 to 1827 it is the only one at Weston.
FreeREG, Weston: James, son of JOSEPH and SARAH WALLIS, labourer; four months after the marriage quarter and three months after the census.

FreeBMD, Hitchin: JOSEPH WALLIS, aged 82, December quarter 1912, vol 3a p729; SARAH WALLIS, aged 56, March quarter 1887, vol 3a p268. A search of Hitchin for Joseph Wallis between 1881 and 1915 returns him and an infant of 1900 only. For Sarah it returns three: aged 56 (1887, her), 82 (1885) and 84 (1885), which are older women. Matched by name and age, not by certificate.

The census ages for Joseph run 23 (1851), and the index's 1829 birth in 1871, against a baptism of 1827 and a death at 82 in 1912 (born 1829 or 1830). Sarah is 21 in 1851 (born 1829 or 1830), 56 at death (1830 or 1831). Nobody has linked Caroline Castle to the Caroline baptised in 1862 by a document. The 1851 marriage certificate would name both fathers, and it is the one purchase that would turn the whole chain from probable to documented.

The generation above Joseph's and Sarah's parents, read from FreeREG (Weston Holy Trinity and Clothall and Wallington St Mary) with the same helper as before. FreeREG is an index of volunteer transcriptions; every entry below is a transcription of a register line and not an image.

record: Wallis, Weston: the marriage of Joseph's grandparents
detail: 13 Oct 1804, Weston: Joseph Wallis, bachelor, and Ann Phillips, spinster, both of Weston; witnesses James Swaine and Robert Hide. Children baptised at Weston to Joseph and Ann Wallis: Jane 2 Jun 1805, William 13 Sep 1807, Esther Philips 6 May 1810. A Joseph Wallis aged 43 was buried at Weston on 6 Apr 1827 and an Anne Wallis aged 48 on 5 Apr 1833. THE MIDDLE NAME OF THE DAUGHTER BORN IN 1810, ESTHER PHILIPS, IS WHAT TIES THE WIFE TO THE PHILLIPS FAMILY BELOW.

James, son of William and Esther Phillips, baptised 19 Sep 1776; Ann, daughter of William and Esther, baptised 16 Nov 1783; a William Phillips, yeoman, buried 20 Oct 1793 (no age given). James Phillips married Sarah Kiddell at Weston on 9 Nov 1796; their children baptised there: Elizabeth 21 Jan 1798 (indexed Philips), William 21 Sep 1800, Jane 1803, Sarah 1806, Mary 1808, James 1812. James Philips was buried at Weston 20 Feb 1825 aged 49, and a Sarah Phillips on 13 May 1832 aged 56. THE MARRIAGE OF WILLIAM AND ESTHER WAS NOT FOUND UNDER PHILLIPS: it is under PHILIPS. See the next row.

record: What follows from it: Joseph and Sarah were second cousins
detail: Ann Phillips (b. 1783) and James Phillips (b. 1776) were brother and sister. Ann's son was William Wallis and James's daughter was Elizabeth Phillips; William Wallis married Mary Foster and Elizabeth Phillips married William Field; their children Joseph Wallis and Sarah Field married each other in 1851. THAT RESTS ON THREE PROBABLE STEPS: that the William Wallis of 1827 is the William of 1807; that the Elizabeth Phillips who married in 1823 is the Elizabeth Philips baptised in 1798; and that the James Philips of 1798 is the James baptised in 1776. Each is the only candidate found at Weston, and each age fits within a year or two. It is not a finding.

Joseph Wallis married Mary Williamson at Clothall on 26 Dec 1771. Children baptised at Clothall: Sarah 29 Mar 1772, Mary 20 Feb 1774, James Feb 1776, Richard 26 Apr 1778, Ann 18 Jun 1780, JOSEPH 5 Jan 1783, Bett 6 Nov 1785, Peggy 15 Mar 1789. Joseph Wallis was buried at Clothall on 24 Nov 1829 aged 82 and a Mary Wallis on 13 May 1814 aged 67. The Joseph of 1783 is the likeliest groom of 1804 because the Joseph buried at Weston in 1827 was 43; the burial age is a year under the baptism. The other Joseph in the index near those years, baptised at Great Munden on 18 Feb 1781 to William and Sarah, married Elizabeth Stains at Great Munden on 5 Nov 1801 and a Joseph Wallis was buried there on 6 Dec 1848: he is another man.

record: Field, Weston: the father of Sarah's father
detail: Thomas Field married Sarah Wallduck at Weston on 19 Mar 1791. Children baptised at Weston to Thomas and Sarah: Sarah 19 Dec 1791, Thomas 14 Apr 1793, Mary 15 Feb 1795, William 19 Mar 1797, David 13 Jan 1799, WILLIAM 24 Jan 1802. A William Field infant was buried on 8 Mar 1798; a Thomas Field, labourer, on 4 Apr 1803; a William Field aged 80 on 29 Aug 1879. A second Field family at Weston, William and Sarah, had a William baptised in 1788 and seven other children from 1793 to 1807; William Field senior, labourer, was buried 2 Sep 1810. THE WILLIAM FIELD WHO MARRIED IN 1823 IS THEREFORE ONE OF THREE: 1788, 1797 or 1802. The 1802 baptism is the better fit if the infant of 1798 was the 1797 William, which the register does not say. David Field, baptised 13 Jan 1799, is the David Field, 51, bricklayer, born Weston, in the 1851 census, and his wife Ann is 50; he would be Sarah's uncle.

Wallduck baptisms at Weston: Thomas 1762, Elizabeth 1764, Mary 1767, John 1768, Ann 1771, Mary 1777. No Sarah Wallduck between 1755 and 1780, so Sarah, who married Thomas Field in 1791, is not one of the six. Thomas Field's own baptism cannot be told from 18 other Thomas Fields baptised in Hertfordshire from 1750 to 1775.

Thomas Foster married Elizabeth South at Wallington on 11 Oct 1793. Children baptised at Wallington to Thomas and Elizabeth Foster: Sarah 16 Mar 1794, Ann 16 Apr 1797, Thomas 30 Jun 1799, Edith 10 Oct 1802, MARY 26 Oct 1806. An Edward Foster and Elizabeth Foster baptised a child at Wallington in Feb 1806, which is another family. Mary's census age in 1851 (42) is two years under the baptism.

The death of William Wallis between May 1848 and March 1851; Joseph Wallis the elder's baptism before 1757 (no result 1735 to 1757); Mary Williamson's baptism; Elizabeth South's baptism; Sarah Wallduck's baptism; the marriage of William Phillips and Esther and Esther's burial; Elizabeth Phillips's death; Mary Wallis's death after 1851; William Field's household in 1851 (FreeCEN returned seven William Fields, none a Weston labourer born about 1800).

record: THIRD SESSION: William and Esther Phillips, 18 October 2026
detail: FreeREG for the register, and Hertfordshire Names Online (Hertfordshire Archives and Local Studies, free, no account) for the licences, wills and poor-law indexes. Both are indexes of transcriptions, not images.

record: Marriage, William Philips and Esther Wright, 21 Feb 1775
detail: FreeREG, Weston Holy Trinity, indexed under PHILIPS with the bride as 'Edther' WRIGHT, which is a transcription slip for Esther: William Philips, bachelor, and Esther Wright, spinster; witnesses John Wright and Wm. Hide; bride, groom and first witness signed with a cross. Hertfordshire Names Online has the same marriage in the register (21 Feb 1775, Esther Wright) and a MARRIAGE LICENCE (William Phillips of Weston and Esther Wright of Weston, 1775, reference AHH20/21). A licence bond or allegation is the application to the archdeacon's court, and has not been read. A William Hide was the witness in 1775 and a Robert Hide in 1804, at the wedding of William and Esther's daughter Ann.

Only two children of William and Esther were found at Weston: James 19 Sep 1776 and Ann 16 Nov 1783. William Phillips, yeoman, was buried at Weston 20 Oct 1793, no age given. No burial for Esther, under Phillips, Philips, Hester, Hesther or Easter, 1783 to 1860. A William Harwood married an Esther Phillips at Weston on 3 Oct 1795, who may be a daughter or may not; no Esther Phillips was baptised at Weston in the register between 1765 and 1785 under either spelling.

A WILL: William Phillips, yeoman, of Weston, 1760, indexed twice (filed will 107HW16 and registered will 16HR150, Archdeaconries of Huntingdon (Hitchin Division) and St Albans). It has NOT been read. A testator of 1760 who was a yeoman of the same parish is the likeliest father of a yeoman of the same name married in 1775, but nothing in the index says so. THE OTHER CANDIDATE, William Philips baptised at Baldock on 6 Jun 1746 to Charles and Eliz Philips, is weaker: no Charles and Elizabeth Phillips marriage was found, and the one Charles Phillips married at Weston in 1762 married a Mary Dawson.

Hester Wright, baptised 27 Dec 1754 at Stevenage to John and Sarah Wright, is the only Esther or Hester Wright baptised in FreeREG's Hertfordshire between 1738 and 1757. The licence says Esther was of Weston, and the first witness at the wedding was a John Wright, so it is possible. It is no more than that.

A maintenance order of 1804 (Quarter Sessions, QSB/17) names a William Phillips of Knebworth as the putative father of a child of a Weston woman. That is a living William Phillips in 1804, not the yeoman of 1793, and nothing links him to this family; he is mentioned so that he is not mistaken for one.

The will itself; the marriage licence bond itself; Esther's baptism and burial; William's baptism; any other children of William and Esther before 1776 or between 1776 and 1783 or after 1783 at Weston.
